# Decide access throughout the token lifecycle

[← All question groups](../index.md) · `security-token-lifecycle` · **Security & Identity** · Catalog level: senior

<p>Questions come from the preserved source notes. Reframing, assessment intent, senior signals and rubrics are editorial interpretations, not verified model answers or universal interviewer expectations. Follow-ups and the combined production exercise are agent additions. Reading this bank creates no learning record, score, completion or review schedule.</p>

## Start with one representative question

[S05-Q002](#S05-Q002)

<p>Which checks must an API perform before accepting a token, and how would you test rejection?</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Explain when a token-based request should be accepted, denied or recovered during its credential lifecycle.</p>

<ul>
<li>Separate authentication, token representation and authorization decisions.</li>
<li>Choose and evaluate claims from API and privacy requirements.</li>
<li>Trace access-token and refresh-token use, including rotation state.</li>
<li>Test expiry, revocation and repeated credential use with bounded expectations.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

No catalog prerequisite. Establish the terms and scenario assumptions in the foundation questions before progressing; a published lesson is not evidence that you know them.

<p>First establish what identity and permission decisions the API needs. Token structure and claims carry information into those decisions; access and refresh contracts extend them through a session. Rotation, expiry and revocation test whether the same trust boundary still holds when credential state changes.</p>

<a id="S05-Q004"></a>

### S05-Q004 · Foundation

<p>How do authentication and authorization differ when a client calls a protected API?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q004](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q004)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q004](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q004)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain authentication versus authorization.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Use one request to explain the two questions a system must answer. Show which decision establishes the caller and which decides whether the requested action is permitted.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Separate identity verification from permission decisions in a request flow.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a protected ASP.NET Core API as context; detailed middleware configuration is outside this question.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains both decisions with the same caller and operation.</li>
<li>Describes a case where the identity is accepted but the operation is refused.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Using “logged in” as a sufficient reason to allow every protected action.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you explain an authenticated caller being denied access to one resource?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q001"></a>

### S05-Q001 · Foundation

<p>What are the parts of a JWT, and what does each part let an API know about the token?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q001](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q001)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q001](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q001)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What are the parts of a JWT?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain the token format before discussing whether a backend should accept it. Keep reading the representation separate from establishing trust.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Describe a token with clear boundaries between representation, identity information and trust.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use a signed JWT as the starting example; state separately if discussing encrypted JWTs.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Names each part and explains its role using one token example.</li>
<li>Identifies which claims require validation rather than treating readable contents as trusted.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Reciting the three part names without explaining what an API can safely infer.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>If someone edits a visible claim, what must the API check before using it?</li>
</ul>

<a id="S05-Q002"></a>

### S05-Q002 · Mechanism

<p>Which checks must an API perform before accepting a token, and how would you test rejection?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q002](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q002)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q002](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q002)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What makes a token valid?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Walk through acceptance checks and the decision that follows them. Explain what “valid” means for this API rather than using it as an unexplained label.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Turn a trust requirement into explicit checks and rejection cases.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Identify the token type, issuing authority, intended API and validation configuration; authorization remains a separate decision. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Explains why each acceptance check belongs to the API trust boundary.</li>
<li>Provides a negative test that distinguishes a readable token from an acceptable token.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Accepting a token because it decodes successfully or contains a familiar user ID.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you test a token issued for a different API?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q006"></a>

### S05-Q006 · Mechanism

<p>How do access tokens and refresh tokens differ in purpose and use during a login session?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q006](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q006)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q006](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q006)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain access tokens versus refresh tokens.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Trace which party presents each token, to whom, and for what decision. The question is about their contracts, not merely comparing expiry durations.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Explain the token lifecycle using distinct actors and trust boundaries.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume an application uses both token types; token format and lifetime are issuer-specific choices.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces each token through the API and identity-provider interactions.</li>
<li>Explains the impact of losing each token and how the design limits that impact.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Describing the two tokens only as short-lived and long-lived copies of one another.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should the application do when renewal fails?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q007"></a>

### S05-Q007 · Mechanism

<p>Explain refresh-token rotation from one successful renewal to the next, including the state the issuer must track.</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q007](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q007)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q007](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q007)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How does refresh-token rotation work?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Rotation means changing the refresh credential during renewal. Focus on the sequence and concurrent or repeated uses, not just the phrase “issue a new token.”</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Reason about credential state transitions and a race at renewal time.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>State the issuer’s rotation and reuse policy; clients may have multiple simultaneous requests. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces old and new credentials and the resulting server-side state.</li>
<li>Identifies a concurrent-renewal case and a test that checks its expected outcome.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Assuming replacing the client’s stored token alone defines a safe rotation protocol.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What should happen if two tabs renew with the same credential?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q003"></a>

### S05-Q003 · Application

<p>What information would you put in token claims for an application, and how would you decide what to leave out?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q003](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q003)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q003](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q003)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> What information belongs in claims?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>A claim is an assertion carried by the token. Discuss the information its consumers need and the consequences of including unnecessary or changing data.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose an identity contract from consumer needs and privacy constraints.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Assume several APIs consume the token; clarify audience, data sensitivity and how often permissions change.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Connects each proposed claim to a consumer requirement.</li>
<li>Explains how privacy and stale information affect the design and its verification.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Treating a token as a convenient container for the entire user profile.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What happens when a permission changes while an existing token is still usable?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q005"></a>

### S05-Q005 · Application

<p>When would you use roles, permissions or authorization policies to control API access?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q005](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q005)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q005](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q005)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> Explain role-based and policy/permission-based authorization.

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Compare ways to express who may perform an operation. Use a concrete access rule rather than debating the labels in isolation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Choose an authorization model and defend how it handles a changing access rule.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Clarify tenant or resource ownership if it matters; a policy here means an explicit rule for deciding access.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Shows how the chosen model represents one real rule and its exceptions.</li>
<li>Explains what evidence would reveal overly broad or inconsistent access.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Listing role names without addressing resource ownership or changing requirements.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you test that a user cannot access another tenant’s resource?</li>
</ul>

</details>

<a id="S05-Q008"></a>

### S05-Q008 · Failure cases

<p>How would you handle token expiry, revocation and unexpected token reuse without confusing the three events?</p>

**Source:** [S05-Q008](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q008)

<p class="scope-note">Version-sensitive scope: state the actual runtime/framework/provider and check official documentation before making technical claims. This question bank does not certify current behavior, product defaults or performance results.</p>

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S05-Q008](../../sources/05-security-cloud-devops.md#q008)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> How should token expiry, revocation and reuse be handled?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Explain what stops a credential from being accepted, how that decision reaches consumers, and what the client should do next.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Design failure and recovery behavior across the token lifecycle.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Separate access-token and refresh-token handling; establish logout, compromise-response and propagation requirements. Establish the deployed version/provider and consult official documentation before answering.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Distinguishes normal expiry from deliberate revocation and suspected credential reuse.</li>
<li>States a propagation boundary and tests the period before every consumer sees the change.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Promising immediate invalidation everywhere without explaining consumer state or issuer guarantees.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>How would you verify that a revoked session cannot renew access?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A SPA makes concurrent API requests as its session approaches expiry. One tab renews credentials while another retries, and an administrator changes the caller’s permissions. Draw token and permission states, explain how the application should respond to each outcome, and define tests for renewal and refusal. Specify the issuer’s documented policy without inventing immediate global revocation guarantees.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Explains token parts, identity versus permission and the purpose of access and refresh tokens.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Traces acceptance and renewal state across actors, defends claim and permission choices, and checks expiry, reuse and propagation boundaries with evidence.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>Decoding a token, showing a login screen or successfully renewing once does not establish validation, authorization or safe concurrent renewal.</p>
